tags.inscription: This tablet to the memory of Sir Stamford Raffles to whose foresight and genius Singapore owes its existence and prosperity was unveiled on February 6th 1919, the 100th anniversary of the foundation of the settlement.

tags.inscription: 1909-1944. Major-General Lim Bo Seng was born on 27th April, 1909 in Nan-An, Fukien, China. He came to Singapore at the age of 16. After studying at Raffles Institution and Hong Kong University he inherited his father's business in Malaya. Since 1937 ...
tags.name: Lim Bo Seng Memorial

This sculpture shows Scotsman, Alexander Laurie Johnston, a prominent merchant of early Singapore, mediating between a Chinese trader and a Malay Chief, whilst Indian and Chinese coolies load sacks onto a bullock cart - a common sight around the river.
tags.name: The River Merchants

tags.description: Bears its flowers and fruits on thick long stalks that grow directly from the tree trunk. The large, fleshy flowers are attractive and fragrant. Its fruits are round and hard, resembling cannon balls, hence its common name.
Philipino national hero (1861-1896). Quote: "There can be no tyrants where there are no slaves". Visited Singapore on his way to Spain.

tags.description: Brazilian Ironwood (Libidibia ferrea) originates from tropical America. It can grow up to 20 m. The bark patches resemble a leopard's hide, hence the other common name, Leopard Tree.
